clue.text: Remember everything taking place behind play area

indicators.note: taking place behind puts the word for everything after the play area

parts.note: a rec is a recreation ground, a public playing field
everything means all

explanation.surface: A child recalls everything that happened behind the playground.
explanation.definitionFit: To remember something is to bring it back to mind, a plain synonym.

clue.text: I keep telling you, it's a firearm

definitions.meaning: said by someone who says the same thing again and again
a gun that fires several shots without reloading

explanation.surface: An exasperated speaker insists the object is a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A repeater is one who repeats themselves, and also a gun firing several rounds in succession.

clue.text: Ambitious type, Conservative, always is outwardly cunning

indicators.note: outwardly means the word for cunning goes round the outside of the others

parts.note: art can mean cunning or trickery, as in artful
e'er is a poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A Tory careerist is always crafty on the outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A careerist puts personal advancement above everything, an ambitious sort.

clue.text: Harmful drug — not cocaine — creating a type of fever

indicators.note: not means the letter for cocaine is taken away

parts.note: Class A is the most harmful category of drugs under UK law
C is slang shorthand for cocaine

explanation.surface: A dangerous drug, cocaine excepted, brings on a fever.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain drugs are graded by harm, Class A being the worst.
explanation.definitionFit: Lassa fever is a viral haemorrhagic fever first identified in Nigeria.

clue.text: Trawl netting most of favourite type of fish

indicators.note: netting means catching inside, so the search surrounds the shortened favourite

parts.note: to trawl through something is to search it

indicators.note: most of drops the final letter of the word for favourite

parts.note: a favourite is a pet, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A fishing boat drags its net, catching mostly its favourite kind of fish.
explanation.definitionFit: The sea perch is a name for various marine fishes resembling the freshwater perch.

clue.text: Read all on page reproduced by this writer

definitions.text: Read all on page reproduced by this writer

indicators.note: reproduced means made again in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Every page of this author's work deserves reading.
explanation.definitionFit: The American writer of tales of mystery and horror, whose words could be reproduced on any page.

clue.text: Old noble showing where mate's buried?

parts.note: a mate is a pal, so mate's gives pal's
where someone is buried is their grave

explanation.surface: An aristocrat reveals where his friend lies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'where mate's buried' reads as a mate's grave.
explanation.definitionFit: A palsgrave was a count palatine, a German nobleman of former times.

clue.text: French musician not good for the Stones

indicators.note: not means the letter for good is removed

parts.note: gravel is a mass of small stones

explanation.surface: A French musician dismisses the Rolling Stones as not good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Stones' suggests the rock band but means gravel.
explanation.definitionFit: Maurice Ravel was a French composer, best known for Boléro.

clue.text: Girl or boy showing merriment without it

indicators.note: without means the word it is taken out

parts.note: hilarity is great merriment
taken as written

explanation.surface: A child shows no glee at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilary is a first name given to both sexes.

clue.text: One crushed by missile, coming to grief

indicators.note: crushed by means held tightly inside, so one sits within the missile

parts.note: the Pershing was a US ballistic missile
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Someone is flattened by a missile and dies.
explanation.definitionFit: To perish is to die or be destroyed, so coming to grief describes it.

clue.text: I snack half-heartedly after catching train? Impossible to say

indicators.note: catching means the shortened snack wraps round the train
half-heartedly removes half of the doubled middle of the word for snack

parts.note: to nibble is to snack
an express is a fast train

explanation.surface: Someone nibbles listlessly after catching a train.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' drops one of the two central Bs in NIBBLE, leaving NIBLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Inexpressible means beyond words, impossible to put into speech.

clue.text: Somewhere to go: a large Canadian city

parts.note: a lav, short for lavatory, is a place where one goes
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A travel tip naming a big city in Canada worth a visit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Somewhere to go' reads as a destination but is a euphemism for a toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: Laval is a large city in Quebec, near Montreal.

clue.text: In retrospect, say, region round Virginia's capital is nothing special

indicators.note: in retrospect means looking back, so the whole assembly is read backwards

parts.note: say, meaning for example, is abbreviated eg

indicators.note: round means the word for region surrounds the letter that follows

parts.note: a region is an area

indicators.note: capital means the initial letter of Virginia

explanation.surface: Looking back, a region around Virginia's capital turns out to be unremarkable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In retrospect' turns the whole assembly, EGAREVA, back to front, not just the first piece; the comma hides that 'say' is wordplay rather than a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something ordinary or middling, neither good nor bad, is nothing special.

clue.text: Serviceman's uniform

definitions.meaning: a professional soldier in a standing army, as opposed to a reservist
even and consistent, the same throughout

explanation.surface: A soldier's kit described.
explanation.definitionFit: A regular is a career soldier; regular also means even and consistent in pattern.

clue.text: Special pianos should be properly tuned, they believe

indicators.note: tuning an instrument rearranges its parts, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Fancy pianos ought to be kept in tune.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Episcopal Church are believers, people holding a religious faith.

clue.text: Man copied out summaries of works

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man made copies of brief digests of works.
explanation.definitionFit: Compendia, plural of compendium, are concise collections summarising a larger body of work.

clue.text: Greek character trapped in minor fire

indicators.note: trapped in means the Greek letter goes inside the word for minor

parts.note: slight means minor
eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: A Greek man is caught in a small blaze.
explanation.definitionFit: To fire something is to ignite it, to make it burn.

clue.text: God denied by old, clever philosopher

indicators.note: denied by means the god loses the letter for old

parts.note: Pluto is the Roman god of the underworld
arch means slyly clever

explanation.surface: A shrewd old thinker rejects a god.
explanation.definitionFit: Plutarch was a Greek philosopher and biographer of the first century.

clue.text: Highly-strung intellectual backing painting technique

indicators.note: backing means supporting from behind, so the intellectual word comes after the technique

parts.note: tempera is painting with pigment bound in egg yolk
mental means of the intellect

explanation.surface: A brainy type champions a particular way of painting.
explanation.definitionFit: A temperamental person is moody and easily upset, the same as being nervy and tense.

clue.text: Plant in graduate's workplace shooting upwards

indicators.note: in a down clue shooting upwards means the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: an MA is a Master of Arts graduate, so graduate's is MA's
a lab is a scientist's workplace

explanation.surface: A plant grows fast in a graduate student's laboratory.
explanation.definitionFit: Balsam is a flowering plant, such as Himalayan balsam.

clue.text: Fishermen using line in French city

indicators.note: in places the letter for line inside the city name

parts.note: Angers is a city on the Loire in western France

explanation.surface: Anglers cast their lines in a French city.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglers are people who fish with a rod and line.

clue.text: Paint — gallons oddly used on front of store

indicators.note: oddly takes the odd-numbered letters of gallons
front of takes the first letter of store

explanation.surface: Paint is used by the gallon on a shop front.
explanation.definitionFit: Gloss is a type of shiny paint.

clue.text: Short drama: Pinter's first, a telly production

indicators.note: first picks out the opening letter of the playwright's name
a production makes something anew, so these letters are reworked into another order

explanation.surface: A short TV drama by Harold Pinter, his first made for the small screen.
explanation.definitionFit: A playlet is a brief play, the diminutive of play.

clue.text: Article run by Sun about crime

parts.note: a is the indefinite article
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
S is the abbreviation for Sunday
on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: A newspaper article run by The Sun about a crime.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sun is a British tabloid, but here Sun is short for Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson, deliberately setting fire to property, is a criminal offence.

clue.text: Duellist initially argues about weapon

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word for argues is read backwards

parts.note: to row is to quarrel, so argues means rows

indicators.note: initially takes the first letter of duellist

explanation.surface: A duellist begins by disputing the choice of weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: A sword is a bladed weapon, the classic one in a duel.

clue.text: Sweet stuff and grease mixed with half portion of butter

indicators.note: mixed means stirred together, so the letters are rearranged
half portion of keeps the first three of the six letters of butter

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: blend something sweet with grease and half the butter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugar refined from sugar beet is a sweetener, hence sweet stuff.

clue.text: Lots of people, old, given hands-on experience?

parts.note: a mass is a large crowd of people
aged means old

explanation.surface: A crowd of elderly people are given practical training.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hands-on experience' suggests practical training; taken literally it is being rubbed by hands, which the question mark flags.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone massaged has literally had hands worked over their body, a playful reading of hands-on.

clue.text: Robbery: heartless sin at church

indicators.note: heartless removes the middle of sin, leaving its outer letters

explanation.surface: A robbery in church is a cruel sin.
explanation.definitionFit: A snatch is a quick theft, as in a bag snatch.
